title: Hell Creek Formation
summary: The Hell Creek Formation is a body of freshwater clays, mudstones and sandstones laid down in the last part of the Cretaceous, exposed in eastern Montana and nearby states. Its dinosaur beds, including Tyrannosaurus and Triceratops, and the K-Pg boundary above them record life just before the end-Cretaceous extinction.

uncertainty.note: Rock age range as given by Smithsonian Magazine; UCMP places deposition in the Maastrichtian.

as_recorded.value: between 66 million and 68 million years old

where.historical_name: not applicable (Late Cretaceous landmass, now North America)

importance.justification: Key fossil-bearing unit for latest Cretaceous dinosaurs and the K-Pg boundary; source of most T. rex museum specimens.
